purpose: Gate C: diagnose the existing abundance kernels at the measurement level before selecting a replacement or running gene discovery.
models: Existing binomial likelihood with Beta(C+h,N-C+h) abundance posterior, h=1 and h=0.5. The Poisson/Gamma limit is a diagnostic, not a newly selected kernel. No prior or dispersion is fitted.
target: Fixed underlying gene fraction p and normalized abundance A=(N/s)*p. Counts and total N are integers. Each patient retains unit probability mass. Condition on known supplied exposures to isolate measurement behavior; no RLE fitting or uncertainty propagation in this study.
observed_checks: Mean, median, mode, variance, central 95% and upper 95% bounds. Compare with C/s and the h/s low-count shift. Transform the whole kernel to log2(1+A), checking 128/256 Gauss-Legendre nodes; compare E[log2(1+A)] with log2(1+E[A]). Cross-check current BetaKernelArea means/CDFs.
repeated_counts: Sum binomial probabilities over a range leaving at most 1e-11 probability in each tail. Report unconditional bias/RMSE, central-interval and upper-bound coverage, expected interval width and average kernel variance. Also report observed-count strata 0, 1, 2-9, 10-99, >=100 as conditional diagnostics. Structural p=0 is a boundary, not the primary all-positive model claim.
numerics: Reuse checked inverse Beta CDF with 1e-7 absolute round-trip tolerance. Preserve repairs and largest residual. Probability-sum checks at 5e-8; source and output hashes; never silently drop failed numerical cells.
composition: For exhaustive disjoint count categories, sum posterior fraction means and compare with 1. Check the identity (N+G*h)/(N+2*h) and its depth dependence. This concerns gene-fraction coherence, not patient weighting. Derive coherent joint-model constraints without selecting a new prior.

predictive.procedure: Fresh independent binomial training and future counts at the same true fraction. Compare posterior beta-binomial prediction, plug-in binomial prediction C/N, and known-p oracle. Report held-out log loss with Monte Carlo standard error, explicitly recording impossible plug-in outcomes; zero/nonzero-event Brier score and zero-training stratum. Average scores, never p-values. Do not infer predictive adequacy from width alone.

technical_overdispersion.procedure: Fixed source fraction p; independent preparation fraction P~Beta(p*k,(1-p)*k), k=(1-p)/(p*cv^2)-1, followed by C~Binomial(N,P). Assess unchanged binomial-Beta kernels against both source p and realized preparation P. This isolates technical overdispersion; neither its size nor any biological dispersion is estimated from patients. Report Monte Carlo uncertainty.

prior_self_consistency.procedure: Draw p from the exact Beta(h,h) prior and C~Binomial(N,p). Check posterior CDF ranks and central coverage. This tests computational self-consistency and is explicitly not a biologically realistic RNA-seq validation.

decision: Do not choose h or a new model from this diagnostic. Distinguish numerical correctness, Bayesian prior-averaged consistency, fixed-truth coverage, predictive adequacy, compositional coherence and downstream distribution estimation. Numerical failures must be resolved or marked incomplete; unfavorable scientific behavior must be reported. No production, FDR, biomarker or release claim.
